title: Assistant tool lockdown and hostile-document hardening
acceptance: cargo test -p pdfxi-assistant; the session ruleset is deny-everything plus the five read-only document tools, the read-back is exact or the session is deleted, the version gate refuses non-2.3.x before POST /api/session, document text is budgeted and fenced, and the live negative injection test (ignored by default) shows zero tool calls and no file write
notes: Security half of the assistant pair, opened to unblock T-0253's citation dependency. The assistant session may call only PDFXI's read-only document tools: document_info, page_text, search, selection and outline. No shell, file, edit, web or permission-bypassing tool is exposed, and the session is configured with a ruleset that denies everything else explicitly rather than relying on tool absence. Document text is untrusted tool output: cap its size per call and per conversation, fence it in prompts, and never treat it as instructions. Nothing is sent until the user asks, and the UI must state what is sent (document text, page range, model). Negative test: a fixture PDF whose text contains injected instructions must prove from the session log and event stream that no other tool ran, no file was written, no network destination changed and no permission was bypassed. This task also owns orchestration/blockers/** so it can record discovered escape behaviour. Runs after T-0251 and before T-0253 consumes citations. If session permission rulesets cannot be shown to restrict tools to the five PDFXI document tools, fall back to `POST /api/experimental/generate/text` with pasted size-capped excerpts and no MCP tools; record which mode shipped and why.
